views.name: ball_event
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.team_batting,
  b.team_bowling,
  b.striker_batting_position,
  b.striker,
  b.non_striker,
  b.bowler,
  COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
  er.extra_type,
  COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0) AS extra_runs,
  wt.player_out,
  wt.kind_out
FROM ball_by_ball AS b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN extra_runs AS er
  ON er.match_id = b.match_id
  AND er.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND er.over_id = b.over_id
  AND er.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN wicket_taken AS wt
  ON wt.match_id = b.match_id
  AND wt.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND wt.over_id = b.over_id
  AND wt.ball_id = b.ball_id
views.description: One-row-per-delivered-ball event combining ball_by_ball with batsman_scored, extra_runs, and wicket_taken where available. Use this as the canonical event-level relation for analyses that need runs, extras, and wicket info together. | Use for: ball-level scoring (runs + extras) and wicket summaries; bowler or batsman per-ball analyses; match innings scoring patterns and over-level aggregates

views.name: player_profile
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_id,
  player_name,
  dob,
  batting_hand,
  bowling_skill,
  country_name
FROM player
views.description: One-row-per-player canonical profile. Use to join player attributes (name, batting_hand, bowling_skill, country_name) into match-level or event-level analyses. | Use for: player demographic lookups; grouping players by batting_hand or bowling_skill; age-based analyses when joined with match.match_date

views.name: match_with_teams
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.match_id,
  m.match_date,
  m.season_id,
  m.venue,
  m.team_1,
  t1.name AS team_1_name,
  m.team_2,
  t2.name AS team_2_name,
  m.toss_winner,
  tw.name AS toss_winner_name,
  m.toss_decision,
  m.win_type,
  m.win_margin,
  m.outcome_type,
  m.match_winner,
  mw.name AS match_winner_name,
  m.man_of_the_match
FROM match AS m
LEFT JOIN team AS t1 ON t1.team_id = m.team_1
LEFT JOIN team AS t2 ON t2.team_id = m.team_2
LEFT JOIN team AS tw ON tw.team_id = m.toss_winner
LEFT JOIN team AS mw ON mw.team_id = m.match_winner
views.description: One-row-per-match with explicit team role columns joined to team names for team_1, team_2, toss_winner, and match_winner. Use when readable team names for match roles are needed. | Use for: match listing with human-readable team names; filtering matches by venue, season, toss_decision or winners; aggregations by team across matches

views.name: player_match_roster
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.match_id,
  pm.player_id,
  p.player_name,
  pm.role,
  pm.team_id
FROM player_match AS pm
LEFT JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = pm.player_id
views.description: One-row-per-player-per-match showing the player's role and team in that match plus player_name. Useful to link participants to matches and to join into event-level analyses. | Use for: who played in a match and what role they had; joining player names into event-level (ball) analyses; counting appearances per player or per team

views.name: batting_aggregate_by_player_match
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.striker AS player_id,
  SUM(COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0)) AS runs_scored,
  SUM(CASE WHEN er.extra_type IS NOT NULL THEN COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0) ELSE 0 END) AS extras_on_ball,
  COUNT(*) AS balls_faced
FROM ball_by_ball AS b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN extra_runs AS er
  ON er.match_id = b.match_id
  AND er.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND er.over_id = b.over_id
  AND er.ball_id = b.ball_id
WHERE b.striker IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.striker
views.description: Per-player-per-match batting aggregates computed from ball-level events: total runs (batsman runs), total extras faced by that batsman not included (kept as separate), and balls_faced (count of event rows where the player was striker). Use for match-level batting performance summaries. | Use for: player match-by-match batting performance; strike rate and consistency calculations when joined with match innings totals; filtering top scorers per match

views.name: bowling_aggregate_by_player_match
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.bowler AS player_id,
  COUNT(*) AS balls_bowled,
  SUM(COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0)) AS runs_conceded,
  SUM(CASE WHEN wt.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wickets
FROM ball_by_ball AS b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN extra_runs AS er
  ON er.match_id = b.match_id
  AND er.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND er.over_id = b.over_id
  AND er.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN wicket_taken AS wt
  ON wt.match_id = b.match_id
  AND wt.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND wt.over_id = b.over_id
  AND wt.ball_id = b.ball_id
WHERE b.bowler IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.bowler
views.description: Per-bowler-per-match aggregates: balls_bowled (count of events where bowler delivered), wickets (count of wicket events credited to that delivery), runs_conceded (sum of batsman runs + extras). Use for match-level bowling analysis. | Use for: match-level bowling figures (overs, runs, wickets); economy and strike rate calculations when combined with balls_bowled; comparing bowlers within a match or across matches

views.name: match_innings_scorecard
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  SUM(COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0)) AS total_runs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN wt.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_wickets,
  COUNT(*) AS total_balls
FROM ball_by_ball AS b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN extra_runs AS er
  ON er.match_id = b.match_id
  AND er.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND er.over_id = b.over_id
  AND er.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN wicket_taken AS wt
  ON wt.match_id = b.match_id
  AND wt.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND wt.over_id = b.over_id
  AND wt.ball_id = b.ball_id
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no
views.description: One-row-per-match-per-innings with aggregated innings totals: total_runs (batsman runs + extras), total_wickets, total_balls (delivered). Use for innings-level summaries and match scoring patterns. | Use for: innings totals and run rate calculations; comparing innings across matches or seasons; identifying high-scoring innings or quick collapses

views.name: player_career_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.player_id,
  SUM(pbat.runs_scored) AS total_runs,
  SUM(pbat.balls_faced) AS total_balls_faced,
  SUM(pbowl.wickets) AS total_wickets,
  SUM(pbowl.balls_bowled) AS total_balls_bowled
FROM (
  SELECT
    striker AS player_id,
    COALESCE(SUM(bs.runs_scored),0) AS runs_scored,
    COUNT(*) AS balls_faced
  FROM ball_by_ball AS b
  LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS bs
    ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
    AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
    AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
    AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
  WHERE b.striker IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY striker
) AS pbat
INNER JOIN (
  SELECT
    bowler AS player_id,
    COUNT(*) AS balls_bowled,
    SUM(CASE WHEN wt.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wickets
  FROM ball_by_ball AS b
  LEFT JOIN wicket_taken AS wt
    ON wt.match_id = b.match_id
    AND wt.innings_no = b.innings_no
    AND wt.over_id = b.over_id
    AND wt.ball_id = b.ball_id
  WHERE b.bowler IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY bowler
) AS pbowl
  ON pbat.player_id = pbowl.player_id
RIGHT JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = COALESCE(pbat.player_id, pbowl.player_id)
GROUP BY p.player_id
views.description: Player-level career aggregates across all matches present: total_runs, total_balls_faced, total_wickets, total_balls_bowled. Use as a precomputed summary for player leaderboards and trends. | Use for: career leaderboards and top performers; joining career aggregates with player profiles; filtering players by thresholds (e.g., min balls) for rate stats

views.name: over_level_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  SUM(COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0)) AS over_runs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN wt.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS over_wickets,
  COUNT(*) AS balls_in_over
FROM ball_by_ball AS b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN extra_runs AS er
  ON er.match_id = b.match_id
  AND er.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND er.over_id = b.over_id
  AND er.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN wicket_taken AS wt
  ON wt.match_id = b.match_id
  AND wt.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND wt.over_id = b.over_id
  AND wt.ball_id = b.ball_id
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id
views.description: One-row-per-match-per-innings-per-over summarizing runs and wickets in that over. Useful for over-by-over momentum and boundary analyses. | Use for: over-by-over scoring trends; identifying high-scoring or wicket-rich overs; bowler over performance when joined with bowler info

views.name: players_in_match_count
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.match_id,
  pm.team_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pm.player_id) AS players_in_team_in_match
FROM player_match AS pm
GROUP BY
  pm.match_id,
  pm.team_id
views.description: Count of distinct players per match and per team in that match. Useful for roster completeness checks and substitution analyses. | Use for: verifying playing XIs and substitutes; joining roster counts to match outcomes or team performance
